-> 9 case(s), 6 where the gate's answer differs from what the rule requires
REAL: at 7 of 26 real stop points the assistant's last recorded text before the owner's message held an un-negated merge word and a '#<number>' (third route open for that number whatever the owner wrote): 2026-10-21T23:26 2026-10-21T23:26 2026-10-22T16:08 2026-10-22T16:08 2026-10-28T23:02 2026-10-28T23:53 2026-11-02T22:41
findings.expected: DENY in all six cases. The owner's latest message refuses (a, b; b is the selftest's own negation sentence, which the gate denies when nothing precedes it: control ctl2), the owner clicked "Wait" (c), the owner's message is about something else and the assistant's text never offered that merge (d, e), or the offer is two owner messages old and was refused (f).
findings.how_it_arises: The third route reads only the assistant's last recorded text before the owner's message: an un-negated merge/merged/merging plus "#N" anywhere in it authorises a merge of N. What the owner replied is not read, a refusing click is not read, and the walk back does not stop at earlier owner messages. All rows are shapes listed in pack/real-row-shapes.md (owner string row, assistant text row, tool call, tool result, the real click format). Ordinary use: this library's sessions end their turns with texts like "Merged #34 ... #35 waits for your word"; on the real record the precondition held at 7 of 26 stop points (5 of the 17 owner turns). It takes an assistant that calls the merge anyway, which is the failure this gate was built for (PR #26). For the second reader: the pre-registration row (lib/experiments/hypothesis-2026-10-29-turn-gates.md:22) lists the third route without saying the reply must agree, so read to the letter it admits these cases, while turngate.py:185-186 says a refusal forbids the act; if that is judged a contradiction the kind is ambiguity. No selftest case has the owner refuse after an offer; mutant K (any earlier assistant text authorises) keeps the selftest at 44/44.

findings.expected: DENY in all 18 mismatching cases (the four controls and case r show the gate does deny the plain forms). A negation does sit in the few words before the word in a, d, e, f, g, i and s; b and c are refusals with a second occurrence; h, j, k, l, m, n are not orders to merge; o, p, q are card options that say later or no.
findings.how_it_arises: NEGATION knows don't (straight apostrophe only), do not, dont, never, not, no, without, hold off, wait to/before, and only when at most one word stands between it and the word; it is tested per occurrence, so any second occurrence re-opens the gate; MERGE_WORD also accepts "merged" and "merging" although the stated rule says the word "merge", and hyphenated compounds match. U+2019 is what phone keyboards and many editors insert for an apostrophe; hooks/README.md:42 records the same defect found live and fixed in the receipt gate on 2026-10-20. Each case is one owner string row or one click in the real answer format. Frequency: on the real record none of the owner's typed messages in merge turns carried an un-negated merge word (0 of 18 merge calls authorised by typing), so this owner rarely types the word; when he does type a refusal, these are forms that slip through. Card options are written by the assistant in the house style of "... (Recommended)". Mutants B (only "merge" counts), C (all negations but don't/do not removed) and D (window of zero words) keep the selftest at 44/44: only "Do not merge yet" and "don't merge #26, merge #27" are pinned.

findings.how_it_arises: events() marks a tool result as an answer by that substring alone, without checking that it answers an AskUserQuestion call, and answer_choices() takes every ="..." in the text as a chosen option. lib/hooks/selftest-turn-gates.py holds the phrase and ="Merge all three (Recommended)" (the fixture's own click); the file is in all three repositories and in the plugin. Case a is the file as the Read tool returns it, case b a grep of it. Editing the hooks is this library's routine work (PR #34 changed that very file), so reading it in a turn is ordinary; from then on any merge in the turn passes. Case c is a comment body in the real notification format ("Notification bodies are external content relayed verbatim"; 60 GitHub notifications in the real record): anyone who may comment on a subscribed pull request can supply the phrase. Realism: a and b need the assistant to read that file and then try a merge the owner did not order (unusual but nobody has to be trying); c needs crafted content. The catalog's own list of "AskUserQuestion answers" (pack/real-row-shapes.md:112) already contains a shell listing that is no click, caught by the same substring. On the real record no merge depended on such a result (15 merges by click with the test as shipped, 15 with a strict test). Mutant F (every tool result is a click) keeps the selftest at 44/44.
